analysis.title: GS Feiler - GS Consumer: 3 Key Themes
key_insights: Many consumer bellwethers report over the next few days. AS, HD and VIK report 11/17, with more on Wednesday and Thursday.
Investors have been shorting the Staples sector heavily as it makes all-time highs. XLP hit another all-time high on 11/16, up 10% over the last month and 21% YTD.
GS PB data shows Staples were 6-1 better for sale last week, led almost entirely by shorts and spread across Staples sub-sectors. Investors are fighting the move rather than embracing it.
Staples strength is described as largely one big market momentum trade, with better 3Q earnings in much of HPC and Beauty as a secondary driver.
Feiler expects more beats than misses in Retail EPS over the next 2 weeks. The AS and HD beats on 11/17 were expected, and both raised the sales guide.
Feiler expects strong results from TGT, LOW, WMT, WSM, ROST and BJ. TJX faces the hardest client sentiment for 3Q, with consistent feedback that the quarter was choppy.
Expectations for the following week are for upside at BBY, KSS and ANF.

Discretionary was one of only 3 sub-sectors bought last week. November is historically the best month of the year for Retail, with most of the 10-year outperformance coming in the last 2 weeks of the month (Black Friday).

HD beat and raised its sales guide to the top of the prior range. HD and LOW have held up well despite high-profile sell-side downgrades from other firms, in a very tough housing environment. Feiler's possible reasons: expectations of the HD beat, optimism on housing policy relief (which he doubts), or positioning. LOW reports 11/18.

sector_views.rationale: XLP is at all-time highs, up 10% over the last month and 21% YTD. GS PB data shows heavy short selling into the rally, and the note asks whether to lean into the shorts.
Feiler expects more EPS beats than misses over the next 2 weeks. Late November has strong seasonality, and Discretionary is one of the few sectors with net buying over the last 1.5 weeks.
HD and LOW have held up well in a tough housing environment despite high-profile downgrades. The reasons are unclear.

earnings_insights: HD reported 3Q on 11/17: a beat, with the sales guide raised to the top of the prior range. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
AS reported 11/17: a beat, with the sales guide raised. Feiler says the beat was expected. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
LOW reports 11/18. Investors expected small top-line upside and generally in-line EPS, per Feiler's investor feedback. Feiler expects a strong result.
Feiler expects strong 3Q results from TGT, LOW, WMT, WSM, ROST and BJ. TJX is the hardest client-sentiment setup because of choppy-quarter feedback.
Expectations for the following week are for upside at BBY, KSS and ANF.
Feiler expects far more EPS beats than minimal misses across retail over the next 2 weeks, though not a perfect season.
risk_factors: Staples momentum could continue and squeeze the short positions building into all-time highs.
TJX 3Q sentiment is weak, with consistent investor feedback that the quarter was choppy.
Housing remains very tough, and home improvement stocks are holding up on unclear drivers, including doubtful hopes of housing policy relief.
vol_and_positioning: GS PB data shows Staples were 6-1 better for sale last week, led almost entirely by shorts and spread across sub-sectors.
Staples selling accelerated into all-time highs. Buying came early in the rally about a month ago, and the group has been better for sale for the last 2 weeks.
Discretionary is one of the few sectors with net buying over the last 1.5 weeks, and it was one of only 3 sub-sectors bought last week.
cross_bank_references: HD and LOW have both held in very well, despite some very high profile sell-side downgrades (away from us).
